text_blocks.snippet: Arthritis risk factors include age, sex, genetics, joint injuries, obesity, smoking, and certain health conditions. Some risk factors, like age and genetics, are non-modifiable, while others, like weight and lifestyle, can be managed.
snippet_highlighted_words: age, sex, genetics, joint injuries, obesity, smoking, and certain health conditions

list.title: Age:
list.snippet: The risk of developing most types of arthritis increases with age, especially osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, and gout.

list.title: Sex:
list.snippet: Women are more likely to develop rheumatoid arthritis, while gout is more common in men.

list.title: Genetics:
list.snippet: Certain genes can predispose individuals to arthritis, particularly rheumatoid arthritis.

list.title: Family History:
list.snippet: Having a family history of arthritis increases the likelihood of developing the condition.

list.title: Obesity:
list.snippet: Excess weight puts extra stress on joints, increasing the risk of osteoarthritis, particularly in the knees and hips.

list.title: Joint Injuries:
list.snippet: Past injuries to joints, like those from sports or accidents, can make them more susceptible to developing arthritis later on.

list.title: Smoking:
list.snippet: Smoking is linked to an increased risk of rheumatoid arthritis and can worsen existing arthritis.

list.title: Physical Inactivity:
list.snippet: Lack of physical activity can contribute to weight gain and weaken muscles, both of which increase arthritis risk.

list.title: Occupational Hazards:
list.snippet: Certain jobs involving repetitive movements, heavy lifting, or prolonged kneeling can strain joints and increase the risk of osteoarthritis.

list.title: Infections:
list.snippet: Some infections can trigger reactive arthritis, where the immune system attacks the joints following an infection.

list.title: Autoimmune Diseases:
list.snippet: Conditions like lupus and scleroderma can cause inflammation and damage to joints, increasing the risk of arthritis.

list.title: Diet:
list.snippet: While diet alone isn't a direct cause, a diet high in processed foods and unhealthy fats can contribute to obesity and inflammation, both of which are linked to arthritis.
